citation: Pfenninger, S., Pickering, B. (2018). Calliope: a multi-scale energy systems modelling framework. Journal of Open Source Software 3(29), 825. doi:10.21105/joss.00825
description: Calliope is a multi-scale energy systems modelling framework for building optimisation models of energy supply, conversion, storage and demand. A model is defined entirely in YAML and CSV text files that list technologies, locations, resource potentials and costs; Calliope builds an optimisation problem from them, solves it and returns capacities and dispatch, and can also run in an operational mode that tests a fixed system under different conditions. It is developed by the Calliope project, founded by Stefan Pfenninger and Bryn Pickering, with a community of contributors. The framework is location independent and targets high spatial and temporal resolution at scales from urban districts to entire continents. It is distributed on PyPI (version 0.7.0, September 2026, Python 3.12 or newer) and conda-forge, with source on GitHub and documentation on read-the-docs; results are saved as CSV or NetCDF or analysed in Python with pandas and xarray. It is released under the Apache 2.0 licence, free of charge. Caveats: Calliope formulates an optimisation problem over technologies and locations, not computing electrical power flow physics, so grid constraints are only represented as far as the model files describe them. Simulation uses are capacity planning and optimisation of electricity and heat systems. Related records: it is an alternative to model-pypsa and model-oemof-solph.
